item.title: Magnuson-Stevens Act Provisions; Atlantic Coastal Fisheries Cooperative Management Act Provisions; General Provisions for Domestic Fisheries; Application for Exempted Fishing Permits
item.description:
The National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) announced that it has received a complete application for an Exempted Fishing Permit (EFP) from the Maine Department of Marine Resources (ME DMR) and is taking public comment on it. An EFP lets federally permitted vessels fish outside certain rules for a research project. The proposed project would test acoustic on-demand, timed-release, and spring-release gear retrieval systems, plus gear geolocation technology, in Gulf of Maine trap/pot and gillnet fisheries. The stated goal is to reduce the risk of large whale entanglement in vertical lines. This is a notice with a request for comments, not a final decision.
Effective: not stated in the notice Tags: American lobster, Gulf of Maine, Maine, Federal waters, Greater Atlantic, New England
Original notice: https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/09/14/2026-18629/magnuson-stevens-act-provisions-atlantic-coastal-fisheries-cooperative-management-act-provisions

item.title: Fisheries of the Northeastern United States; Atlantic Bluefish Fishery; Quota Transfer From New Jersey to North Carolina
item.description:
New Jersey is giving part of its 2026 commercial bluefish quota to North Carolina. The National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) approved the swap, which the two states agreed to. The transfer is 250,000 pounds (113,398 kilograms). NMFS says the request came in so North Carolina would not go over its 2026 state quota.
Effective: 2026-09-10 Tags: Bluefish, New Jersey, North Carolina, Mid-Atlantic, Greater Atlantic
Original notice: https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/09/11/2026-18623/fisheries-of-the-northeastern-united-states-atlantic-bluefish-fishery-quota-transfer-from-new-jersey

item.title: Fisheries of the Northeastern United States; Greater Atlantic Region Catch Share Cost Recovery Program Updates
item.description:
The National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) finalized changes to how it bills permit holders for the cost of running three catch share programs in the Greater Atlantic Region. NMFS will now waive any cost recovery fee under $25 and roll that unbilled amount into the next year's accounting. Billing and payment timelines are also made the same across all three programs: bills go out within 6 months after the end of a cost recovery period, and payment is due within 30 days from the bill date. Nothing changed between the proposed rule and this final rule.
Effective: 2026-10-13 Tags: Atlantic sea scallop, Golden tilefish, Atlantic surfclam, Ocean quahog, Greater Atlantic, New England, Mid-Atlantic
Original notice: https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/09/11/2026-18607/fisheries-of-the-northeastern-united-states-greater-atlantic-region-catch-share-cost-recovery

item.title: Atlantic Highly Migratory Species; Schedules for Atlantic Shark Identification Workshops and Protected Species Safe Handling, Release, and Identification Workshops
item.description:
The National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) announced the dates and locations for its next round of free Atlantic Shark Identification Workshops and Safe Handling, Release, and Identification Workshops. Two shark identification sessions are set for October 19 and November 11, 2026, and three safe handling sessions are set for October 14, November 2, and December 3, 2026. This is a scheduling notice only. It restates existing workshop and certificate rules under 50 CFR 635.8 and notes that the online recertification option NMFS added in December 2021 is still available for people who already took an in-person class.

item.title: Fisheries of the Northeastern United States; Monkfish; Framework Adjustment 17
item.description:
The National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) put in place Framework Adjustment 17 to the Monkfish Fishery Management Plan (FMP). It sets monkfish catch limits for fishing year 2026 and projects them for 2027 and 2028. Overall catch limits stay the same as the 2023-2025 levels, but changes in expected discards shift the target total allowable landings down 3 percent in the northern area and up slightly in the southern area. The rule also changes who triggers the overage accountability measure, and it adds default catch limits that carry over the prior year's numbers if new ones are not published in time.
Effective: 2026-09-28 Tags: Monkfish, Gulf of Maine, Georges Bank, Southern New England, Mid-Atlantic, New England, Greater Atlantic, Maine, North Carolina, Federal waters
Original notice: https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/08/27/2026-17500/fisheries-of-the-northeastern-united-states-monkfish-framework-adjustment-17

item.title: Fisheries of the Northeastern United States; Mackerel, Squid, and Butterfish; 2026 Illex Squid Quota Harvested
item.description:
The National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) is closing the directed Illex squid fishery in Federal waters for the rest of 2026. The closure was triggered by a projection that 96 percent of the 2026 domestic annual harvest (DAH), also called the commercial quota, will be caught. During the closure, a 10,000-pound per-trip possession limit applies, along with a limit of one Illex squid landing per calendar day. Federally permitted dealers face a matching 10,000-pound limit on Illex squid received from a vessel. NMFS skipped advance public comment and the usual 30-day wait, saying the data came in only recently and high-volume landings can burn through the quota fast.
Effective: 2026-08-23 Tags: Illex squid, Federal waters, Greater Atlantic
Original notice: https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/08/21/2026-17148/fisheries-of-the-northeastern-united-states-mackerel-squid-and-butterfish-2026-illex-squid-quota

item.title: Fisheries of the Northeastern United States; Summer Flounder Fishery; Quota Transfer From North Carolina to Massachusetts
item.description:
North Carolina and Massachusetts agreed to move a small piece of North Carolina's 2026 commercial summer flounder quota to Massachusetts. The National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) approved the transfer and published the updated 2026 quota numbers for both states. The transfer was requested to repay landings made by an out-of-state permitted vessel under a safe harbor agreement. The underlying rules and the state-by-state allocation process are unchanged.
Effective: 2026-08-20 Tags: Summer flounder, North Carolina, Massachusetts, Mid-Atlantic, New England, Greater Atlantic
Original notice: https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/08/21/2026-17129/fisheries-of-the-northeastern-united-states-summer-flounder-fishery-quota-transfer-from-north

item.title: Atlantic Highly Migratory Species; North Atlantic Swordfish, South Atlantic Swordfish, North Atlantic Albacore, and Atlantic Bluefin Tuna Quotas
item.description:
The National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) put in place 2026 quotas for North Atlantic swordfish, South Atlantic swordfish, North Atlantic albacore tuna, and Atlantic bluefin tuna, based on decisions by the International Commission for the Conservation of Atlantic Tunas (ICCAT). The U.S. baseline bluefin tuna quota rose from 1,316.14 metric tons to 1,509.98 metric tons, and that new total was split among the existing domestic categories using the percentages already in the rules. The pelagic longline bycatch set-aside for bluefin tuna went from 25 metric tons to 62.5 metric tons, and it is now handed out to Individual Bluefin Tuna Quota (IBQ) shareholders with Atlantic-region shares instead of being tracked separately for the Northeast Distant Gear Restricted Area. NMFS also carried forward 2025 underharvest into the 2026 quotas and moved 30.8 metric tons of bluefin tuna quota from the Longline category back to the Reserve category. The rule adds a reference to the new ICCAT North Atlantic swordfish management procedure and deletes some outdated dead-discard language.
Effective: 2026-08-19 Tags: Swordfish, Bluefin tuna, Albacore tuna, Atlantic Ocean, Greater Atlantic, Gulf of America, Caribbean Sea, Northeast Distant Gear Restricted Area
Original notice: https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/08/19/2026-16870/atlantic-highly-migratory-species-north-atlantic-swordfish-south-atlantic-swordfish-north-atlantic

item.title: Atlantic Highly Migratory Species; Revisions to Fishing Gear Regulations
item.description:
The National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) has proposed changes to fishing gear rules for Atlantic highly migratory species (HMS) — sharks, tunas, billfish, and swordfish. The proposal would let buoy gear be set and hauled with power assistance, such as electric or hydraulic winches, instead of by hand only. It would also open buoy gear to more permit types and let more species be kept on it, open speargun gear to more commercial permits for bigeye, albacore, yellowfin, and skipjack (BAYS) tunas, and write bait-collection gear such as cast nets and small dipnets into the rules. This is a proposed rule open for public comment, not a final rule.
Effective: not stated in the notice Tags: Swordfish, Bigeye tuna, Albacore tuna, Yellowfin tuna, Skipjack tuna, Bluefin tuna, Coastal sharks, Atlantic Ocean, Gulf of America, Caribbean Sea, Greater Atlantic, Federal waters, Northeast Distant Gear Restricted Area
Original notice: https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/08/14/2026-16591/atlantic-highly-migratory-species-revisions-to-fishing-gear-regulations

item.title: Atlantic Highly Migratory Species; Atlantic Bluefin Tuna Fisheries; Closure of the Angling Category Gulf of Maine Area Trophy Fishery for 2026
item.description:
The National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) closed the Angling category trophy Atlantic bluefin tuna fishery in the Gulf of Maine area for the rest of 2026. NMFS says landings data show the 2.3 metric ton subquota for that area has been reached and exceeded. Trophy bluefin are large medium and giant fish measuring 73 inches (185 cm) curved fork length or greater. NMFS had already closed the other three trophy areas earlier in 2026, so with this action the trophy bluefin fishery is closed in all areas for the year.
Effective: 2026-08-04 Tags: Bluefin tuna, Gulf of Maine, New England, Atlantic Ocean, Greater Atlantic
Original notice: https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/08/05/2026-15878/atlantic-highly-migratory-species-atlantic-bluefin-tuna-fisheries-closure-of-the-angling-category

item.title: Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act Provisions; Fisheries of the Northeastern United States; Northeast Multispecies Fishery; Framework Adjustment 72
item.description:
The National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) put Framework Adjustment 72 to the Northeast Multispecies (groundfish) Fishery Management Plan into effect as an interim final rule, skipping advance public comment. It sets new status determination criteria for Georges Bank yellowtail flounder, replacing the "unknown" criteria in place since Framework 53. It sets 2026 shared United States/Canada quotas for eastern Georges Bank cod, eastern Georges Bank haddock, and Georges Bank yellowtail flounder, and sets catch limits for 12 groundfish stocks, some for 2026 and some for 2026 through 2030. It also lets the Greater Atlantic Regional Administrator set recreational measures for cod and haddock stocks that have no recreational sub-annual catch limit, and it removes the sector management uncertainty buffer for 2026 for all allocated stocks except Southern New England cod.
Effective: 2026-08-04 Tags: Atlantic cod, Haddock, Yellowtail flounder, Winter flounder, Acadian redfish, White hake, Ocean pout, Atlantic wolffish, Atlantic halibut, Georges Bank, Gulf of Maine, Eastern Gulf of Maine, Western Gulf of Maine, Cape Cod, Southern New England, Mid-Atlantic, New England, Greater Atlantic
Original notice: https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/08/04/2026-15784/magnuson-stevens-fishery-conservation-and-management-act-provisions-fisheries-of-the-northeastern

item.title: Atlantic Highly Migratory Species; Meeting of the Atlantic Highly Migratory Species Advisory Panel
item.description:
The National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) announced a two-day meeting of the Atlantic Highly Migratory Species (HMS) Advisory Panel in September 2026. The panel will discuss options for conserving and managing Atlantic swordfish, shark, tuna, and billfish fisheries. This is a meeting announcement only; it does not change any fishing rules. The meeting is open to the public, in person and online.
Effective: not stated in the notice Tags: Swordfish, Bluefin tuna
Original notice: https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/08/03/2026-15684/atlantic-highly-migratory-species-meeting-of-the-atlantic-highly-migratory-species-advisory-panel

item.title: Agency Information Collection Activities; Submission to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) for Review and Approval; Comment Request; Highly Migratory Species Tournament Registration and Reporting
item.description:
The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) is sending a renewal of its Atlantic highly migratory species (HMS) tournament registration and reporting paperwork to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) for review. The agency is also revising the forms: updating the target species list on the registration form, adding vessel effort reporting by in-state versus out-of-state participants, adding bluefin tuna catch reporting by size class, clarifying which species need individual lengths and weights in post-tournament catch reports, and adding questions about depredation of tournament catch by sharks, other fish, or marine animals. A new tournament operator survey is being added to cover operating costs, income sources, and participant descriptions. The public gets an extra 30 days to comment, after an earlier 60-day comment period that opened on December 19, 2025.
Effective: not stated in the notice Tags: Swordfish, Bluefin tuna
Original notice: https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/22/2026-14708/agency-information-collection-activities-submission-to-the-office-of-management-and-budget-omb-for

item.title: Atlantic Highly Migratory Species; Atlantic Bluefin Tuna Fisheries; Closure of the Harpoon Category Fishery for 2026
item.description:
The National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) closed the Harpoon category fishery for large medium and giant Atlantic bluefin tuna for the rest of the 2026 fishing year. NMFS says reported Harpoon landings reached about 72.8 metric tons, above the adjusted Harpoon quota of 65.6 metric tons. The Harpoon season normally runs June 1 through November 15; this closure ends it early for 2026. NMFS says it may reopen the fishery if it later finds reasonable fishing opportunities, and the category reopens automatically on June 1, 2027.
Effective: 2026-07-17 Tags: Bluefin tuna, Atlantic Ocean, Greater Atlantic
Original notice: https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/20/2026-14592/atlantic-highly-migratory-species-atlantic-bluefin-tuna-fisheries-closure-of-the-harpoon-category

item.title: Atlantic Highly Migratory Species; Atlantic Bluefin Tuna Fisheries; Harpoon Category Quota Transfer
item.description:
The National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) moved 6.4 metric tons (mt) of Atlantic bluefin tuna quota from the Reserve category to the Harpoon category. That raises the Harpoon category quota for 2026 from its baseline of 59.2 mt to 65.6 mt, and drops the Reserve category from 7.4 mt to 1 mt. NMFS says the Harpoon category had already landed about 63.1 mt, so the category was on track to run out of quota. The notice states the Harpoon category fishery will stay open until November 15, 2026, or until the adjusted quota is reached, whichever comes first.
Effective: 2026-07-14 Tags: Bluefin tuna, Atlantic Ocean, Greater Atlantic
Original notice: https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/16/2026-14366/atlantic-highly-migratory-species-atlantic-bluefin-tuna-fisheries-harpoon-category-quota-transfer

item.title: Request for Information on Ropeless Fishing; Fisheries of the Northeastern United States and Atlantic Coastal Fisheries Cooperative Management
item.description:
The National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) published a request for information, not a rule. It is asking fishermen and others with specialized knowledge for input on "ropeless" fishing gear, meaning fixed gear that does not use persistent buoy lines. The notice lays out 52 questions across topics like gear authorization, crew safety, reliability standards, digital gear marking, gear conflict, equity, training, law enforcement, and data governance. NMFS says it plans to summarize the responses and post that summary publicly.
Effective: not stated in the notice Tags: American lobster, Jonah crab, Greater Atlantic, New England, Mid-Atlantic, Federal waters
Original notice: https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/16/2026-14363/request-for-information-on-ropeless-fishing-fisheries-of-the-northeastern-united-states-and-atlantic

item.title: Fisheries of the Northeastern United States; 2026 Chub Mackerel, Squid, and Butterfish Fishery Specifications
item.description:
The National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) finalized the 2026 catch specifications for the Mackerel, Squid, and Butterfish Fishery Management Plan (FMP), as recommended by the Mid-Atlantic Fishery Management Council. For chub mackerel and Illex squid, the 2026 numbers are unchanged from the 2025 rollover levels, and the same numbers are projected for 2027 and 2028. Longfin squid 2026 numbers were reaffirmed unchanged as well. Butterfish is the one real change: most 2026 butterfish numbers are lower than 2025, with the acceptable biological catch (ABC), annual catch limit (ACL), and annual catch target (ACT) down 19 percent and domestic annual harvest (DAH) down 29 percent. Atlantic mackerel was handled in a separate action, Framework Adjustment 17, and is not set by this rule.
Effective: 2026-08-10 Tags: Chub mackerel, Illex squid, Longfin squid, Butterfish, Atlantic mackerel, Mid-Atlantic, Greater Atlantic, New England
Original notice: https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/09/2026-13867/fisheries-of-the-northeastern-united-states-2026-chub-mackerel-squid-and-butterfish-fishery

item.title: Fisheries of the Northeastern United States; Omnibus Management Flexibility Amendment to New England Fishery Management Council Fishery Management Plans
item.description:
The National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) has proposed a rule to put in place the New England Fishery Management Council's Omnibus Management Flexibility Amendment. The proposal would change how often catch specifications are set, letting the Council recommend specifications covering one to five years across all of its fishery management plans (FMPs) instead of the current mix of two-year and three-year cycles. It would create a defined specifications process for the Northeast Multispecies and Monkfish FMPs, which now have to use framework adjustments or amendments, and would extend in-season adjustment authority (already in the Atlantic Herring FMP) to all the Council's FMPs. It would also drop required annual plan development team reviews in the Monkfish and Northeast Skate Complex FMPs and the annual review and report for the small-mesh part of the Northeast Multispecies FMP. NMFS describes the action as administrative and says it would not change current operational fishing rules.
Effective: not stated in the notice Tags: Atlantic sea scallop, Monkfish, Atlantic herring, Atlantic deep-sea red crab, New England, Mid-Atlantic, Federal waters
Original notice: https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/08/2026-13809/fisheries-of-the-northeastern-united-states-omnibus-management-flexibility-amendment-to-new-england

item.title: Atlantic Highly Migratory Species; Atlantic Bluefin Tuna Fisheries; Closure of the Angling Category Southern New England Area Trophy Fishery for 2026
item.description:
The National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) closed the Angling category "trophy" Atlantic bluefin tuna fishery in the Southern New England area for the rest of 2026. NMFS says landings data show the 2.3 metric ton subquota for that area has been reached and exceeded. Trophy fish are large medium and giant bluefin measuring 73 inches (185 centimeters) curved fork length or greater. The trophy fishery in the Gulf of Maine area stays open, and the notice states that catch-and-release and tag-and-release fishing for bluefin of all sizes continues under the programs at 50 CFR 635.26. The closure runs through December 31, 2026.
Effective: 2026-07-03 Tags: Bluefin tuna, Southern New England, New England, Gulf of Maine, Atlantic Ocean, Greater Atlantic
Original notice: https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13630/atlantic-highly-migratory-species-atlantic-bluefin-tuna-fisheries-closure-of-the-angling-category

item.title: Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act Provisions; Fisheries of the Northeastern United States; Northeast Multispecies Fishery; Amendment 25 (Revised)
item.description:
The National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) split Atlantic cod into four stocks instead of two. Instead of Gulf of Maine (GOM) cod and Georges Bank (GB) cod, the Northeast Multispecies Fishery Management Plan (FMP) now uses Eastern Gulf of Maine (EGOM), Western Gulf of Maine (WGOM), Georges Bank, and Southern New England (SNE) cod. The rule writes the new stock boundaries into the regulations and sets status determination criteria, catch limits, sector and common pool allocations, trimester catch areas, common pool trip limits, and recreational seasons, sizes, and bag limits for each of the four stocks. It replaces the default 2026 cod quotas, which had been set at 75 percent of the 2025 levels for the old two stocks. One thing changed from the proposed rule: the May recreational season for WGOM cod was dropped, leaving a September-October season.
Effective: 2026-06-30 Tags: Atlantic cod, Haddock, Atlantic sea scallop, Atlantic herring, Eastern Gulf of Maine, Western Gulf of Maine, Georges Bank, Southern New England, Gulf of Maine, New England, Greater Atlantic, Federal waters
Original notice: https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/30/2026-13153/magnuson-stevens-fishery-conservation-and-management-act-provisions-fisheries-of-the-northeastern

The transfer repays landings made in one state by a vessel permitted in the other under a safe harbor agreement. NMFS is publishing the updated 2026 commercial quota numbers for both states.
